messages.author: 6ef25433d1a8167d
messages.subject: The variable "MAD"
parts:
Dear all,

We figured out the aggregation process, thanks to Ben. However,  we have trouble finding the variable "MAD".

We want to use the variables "ENMO" (Euclidean Norm Minus One with Negative Values rounded to Zero) and "MAD" ( Epoch average of the Euclidean norm per time step minus the average, named Mean Amplitude Deviation) for the analysis of the physical activity of the participants.

We found "ENMO in the output file "basic" but not "MAD".

I wanted to ask whether a change is necessary for the configuration code of the processing or where we can find the "MAD" variable.

Please see the configuration code below:

Configuration Code: GGIR::GGIR( mode = c(1,2,3,4,5), datadir = here::here("data-raw"), outputdir = here::here("output_timeseries"), do.report = c(2,4,5), do.parallel = TRUE,

#===================== # Part 2 #===================== strategy = 1, hrs.del.start = 0, hrs.del.end = 0, maxdur = 9, includedaycrit = 16, qwindow=c(0,24), mvpathreshold =c(100), bout.metric = 6, excludefirstlast = FALSE, includenightcrit = 16, #===================== # Part 3 + 4 #===================== def.noc.sleep = 1, outliers.only = TRUE, criterror = 4, do.visual = TRUE, #===================== # Part for time series #===================== save_ms5rawlevels=TRUE, save_ms5raw_format ="csv", save_ms5raw_without_invalid = FALSE, epochvalues2csv = TRUE, #===================== # Part 5 #===================== threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100), threshold.vig = c(400), boutcriter = 0.8, boutcriter.in = 0.9, boutcriter.lig = 0.8, boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10), boutdur.mvpa = c(1), includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3, #===================== # Visual report #===================== timewindow = c("WW"), visualreport=TRUE)  

Thank you in advance.

Best wishes,

Elif

messages.author: 05de4f382b390d3d
messages.subject: Re: The variable "MAD"
parts:
Hi Elif,

The metric ENMO is calculated by default in GGIR, but this is not the case for MAD. To calculate MAD you need to include "do.mad = TRUE" in your function call and you would need to re-run part 1 as the metrics are calculated in part 1 (make sure you include "overwrite = TRUE").

Best,
Jairo

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: The variable "MAD"
parts:
In addition to Jairo's response, it may be good to mention that GGIR allows you to extract multiple acceleration metrics, e.g. GGIR(do.enmo = TRUE, do.mad = TRUE, do.lfenmo = TRUE, ...)

However, the more metrics you extract the more computationally heavy running GGIR will become. So, it is advisable that you think carefully which metrics you need.

Vincent
